label: original-phase z/1/p/f/o/q input after a y/j/v/e/r/k/g/h/b/l-heavy prefix
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (95% of mass), never at t=0 or on the delimiter, and rarely in the copy phase (where it shows up mainly when the output is y). Rate goes up later in the input (orig_idx 8 is 5.7x). The input token is z (30% of mass), 1, p, f, o or q; those six inputs hold 87% of mass. It is gated by history: the rate goes up when earlier inputs include y, j, v, e, r, k, g, h, b or l, and first_tok=y gives 4.9x lift. The largest activations are z or p late in sequences that start with y. Input token alone is very imprecise (P=0.08). Requiring at least 2 such history tokens gives dev P=0.22, R=0.62, F1=0.33, mass recall 0.75. The history dependence looks like a graded hidden-state direction rather than a clean set rule, so precision stays low. Does not fire on most other inputs (digits 0/2/3, most letters) or on the delimiter.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: z, 1; t=2: z, 1, p, f; t=3: z, 1, p, f) and the first original token (most: y, j, v, e, r, k; least: 1, 2, o, q); timing cues that raise it most: L=8 & t=7, L=9 & t=15, L=4 & t=3.
